question.text: Under the exchange's arbitration mechanism, the maximum time for resolution of a dispute is:

answer.text: 4 months from the date of appointment of the arbitrator, extendable by 2 months with consent of parties
2 years from the date of filing
1 week from the date of filing

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the stock exchanges' arbitration mechanism for investor-broker disputes, the arbitration is expected to be concluded within 4 months from the date of appointment of the arbitrator. Where the matter genuinely requires more time, the period can be extended by up to 2 more months with the consent of the parties. The structured timeline ensures investor disputes are not left open-ended. The Trap: A 2-year window or a "no time limit" rule would defeat the purpose of investor protection. A 1-week resolution is unrealistically short for an arbitration involving evidence and arguments. Note: The specific "4 months from arbitrator appointment, extendable by 2 months" timeline is not stated in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages on ODR/SMARTODR, which instead describe 21-calendar-day conciliation/review and post-award payment/challenge timelines. The framing above reflects general exchange-arbitration practice rather than a workbook citation.
